title: Ferrari CEO hails Tesla Roadster redesign as bold innovation
extract: Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna praised the redesigned Tesla Roadster as an example of the bold innovation the car industry needs. The Roadster presentation included dramatic airborne manoeuvres and SpaceX-derived thrusters; production is planned for 2028.

title: Germany's Agile Robots plans to build up to 2,000 humanoid robots with Nvidia
extract: Agile Robots plans to produce 1,000–2,000 compact humanoid robots in 2027 through a partnership with Nvidia. The research-oriented machines combine Agile's hardware with Nvidia computing and software, aiming to save labs months of integration work.

title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
extract: A political group supported by OpenAI president Greg Brockman is spending millions to back candidates opposed to restrictions on AI development, even as executives call for federal safety rules. The reporting examines the tension between public safety messaging and industry lobbying.

title: Prometheus procfs adds Linux NVMe diagnostic counters
extract: The Prometheus procfs library now parses Linux 7.2 diagnostic counters for NVMe controllers, namespaces and multipath namespace heads. The new on-demand fields expose command errors, retries, reconnects and path-failure behaviour without forcing every caller to read extra sysfs files.

title: MAME Home Systems adds BBC Micro models to its system roster
extract: A new development build lists the BBC Micro Model A, Model B, B+ and Master 128 in the MAME Home Systems core. The project notes that a ROM-based boot test has not yet been performed, so this is a meaningful integration step rather than a claim of complete validation.

title: KliveIDE completes +3 ROM annotations and adds ZX Spectrum Next ROM level 2
extract: The KliveIDE project has completed annotations for the ZX Spectrum +3 ROMs and added level-two annotations for the ZX Spectrum Next ROMs. The work improves the technical documentation available to people exploring and debugging Spectrum firmware.

title: emu198x releases new Amiga emulator package
extract: The emu198x Homebrew tap has advanced its Amiga emulator package to version 0.43.0. The change makes the new emulator release available through the package manager for users running the project on macOS.

title: emu198x BBC Micro emulator package advances to version 0.43.0
extract: A new Homebrew package update brings the emu198x Acorn BBC Micro emulator to version 0.43.0. This is a fresh release update for the headless emulator project, separate from the MAME Home Systems integration work.

title: UP-Term improves Amiga console window pen rendering
extract: UP-Term now draws Amiga pens 0 and 1 using the window's ground colour in a CON: window. It is a small but concrete compatibility improvement for a terminal project targeting Amiga systems.

title: emu198x adds C64 tape autoloading and media selection before boot
extract: The emulator now supports automatically loading Commodore 64 tapes in Fleet and selecting media before the machine boots. The change makes a common home-computer workflow easier to reproduce in the modern emulator.

title: The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch brings Thure Erik Lund into English
extract: Thure Erik Lund's novel, originally published in 1999, arrives in English as a bleakly comic and linguistically inventive portrait of a man railing against modernity. The review connects its Norwegian setting to broader questions about cultural commodification, technology and alienation.

title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House takes its comedy to the screen
extract: The review covers the Ghosts film spin-off, which keeps the British sitcom's playful supernatural comedy while widening its scope. The cast have also discussed the possibility of further stories, including a caveman-themed spin-off.

title: Scream review: Wes Craven's meta-horror remains sharp 30 years on
extract: A new review revisits Scream three decades after the original's arrival, praising how its self-aware slasher conventions still deliver suspense and wit. It is a useful reminder of the influence the film's genre-savvy approach continues to have.

title: You Can See Everything mania lifts viewership for The Dropout
extract: The documentary You Can See Everything has generated enough attention to lift viewership for The Dropout by 186%, according to the report. The story is an unusual look at how a new documentary can send audiences back to an earlier television treatment of the same subject.

title: Spielberg's War of the Worlds forced Americans to look in the mirror
extract: A new essay revisits Steven Spielberg's War of the Worlds as a science-fiction film shaped by American fears and political anxieties. It treats the alien invasion as a lens on human behaviour rather than just a spectacle-driven disaster movie.
